observation: Outdoor temperature normally appeared about every 7 s.
A later interval was about 17 s.
GFA P06 had previously shown occasional 1-2 minute visibility delays.
diagnosis: The upstream scheduler executes all members of a due poll group in one cycle, producing periodic latency spikes for FAST items when NORMAL/SLOW/RARE groups coincide.
The old profile had approximately 32 FAST, 21 NORMAL, 36 SLOW and 55 RARE serial transactions before byte-bit reuse.
ONCE was tied to poll_cycle==0 and upstream forcepoll/reloadpoll reset poll_cycle, so startup-only items could be replayed.
The separate P80 guard issue is fixed in GFA patch helper v1.0.3: transient P80 transport failures no longer erase a previously validated P80=20 identity.

behavior: Initial process-start cycle still seeds a complete snapshot.
Recurring groups are assigned deterministic per-transaction phases.
Completed ONCE is disabled for the remainder of the process lifetime.
forcepoll refreshes recurring groups but not completed ONCE.
Explicit forced datapoint readbacks remain unchanged.

policy: Core burner/pump/GFA process signals remain FAST.
Outdoor temperature and ordinary user setpoints move to NORMAL.
Internal BLR/CFDM values move to DIAG.
Static service/coding values and read-only weekly programs move to ONCE.
Counters and error histories remain RARE.

expected_live_result.goal: Eliminate periodic 15-20 s FAST latency spikes before any olbreath reduction.

next_step: Measure natural MQTT inter-arrival intervals for FAST and NORMAL entities under olbreath=0.15; only then test lower olbreath as a separate controlled change.

first_live_apply_attempt.failure: test_switch_patch fixture indentation did not match the exact fail-closed upstream marker indentation
first_live_apply_attempt.note: The failure was in the synthetic self-test fixture, not in the live splitter scheduler logic.

changes: Corrected all synthetic upstream indentation markers in test_switch_patch.
Made scheduler patch application transactional with complete rollback on failure.
Profile helper now runs all pure patcher self-tests before staging profile/runtime changes.

olbreath_context.interpretation: 0.15 s is an experimental conservative margin inherited from successful mixed VS1/F7/6B hardware probes, not a recovered Viessmann protocol minimum.
olbreath_context.upstream_function_comment: give vitotronic some time between comms to do other things
olbreath_context.next_policy: Keep 0.15 during scheduler validation; if stable, test 0.10 then 0.05 as separate controlled changes.

conclusion: The phased poll scheduler is now live on the production splitter.
The optimized VDensHO1 profile is active and Home Assistant discovery completed successfully.
The next measurement must be passive MQTT cadence observation without forcepoll, before changing olbreath.
